title: CDT Workflow Engine Workflow Map
description: Static, human-editable workflow map data for the reusable .NET workflow engine and API proof of concept.
notes: Portfolio Trade is seed/sample metadata only. Workflow decisions are made from SQL transition metadata.
No MediatR, CQRS, message broker, BPMN, or plugin framework was found.
No InviteUser or invitation implementation was found; the Invite new user workflow is documented as a gap/inferred extension path.
No ToDesktop, Electron, Tauri, or app.todesktop configuration was found; the ToDesktop build workflow is documented as inferred from the repository's build, CI, and source bundle assets.

components.name: External Form or Operator
components.description: A future form UI, API client, developer, CI job, or console operator that starts workflows, opens workflow context, executes actions, or runs operational commands.

components.name: WorkflowEngine.Api
components.description: ASP.NET Core controller API exposing start workflow, get workflow context, and execute workflow action endpoints.

components.name: WorkflowEngine.Console
components.description: Console proof of concept host. Builds configuration and DI, then dispatches commands through CommandRegistry.

components.name: Build, CI, and Source Bundle
components.description: GitHub Actions, solution build, tests, package audit, and self-extracting source bundle scripts used for verification and handoff.

components.name: Actor and Role Resolution
components.description: API-only adapter that resolves user id, display name, and workflow roles from authenticated claims or development headers.

components.name: Application Contracts
components.description: Stable request and response DTOs shared by console, API, tests, and future UI integration.

components.name: Application Orchestration
components.description: Command handlers, validator, normalizer, canonical hasher, result builder, and result serializer. This layer coordinates input validation and service calls without owning EF persistence.

components.name: HTTP Result Mapping
components.description: Maps WorkflowActionResultEnvelope result codes to API ObjectResult responses.

components.name: Domain Constants
components.description: Small domain project currently holding workflow constants such as the configured connection-string name.

components.name: Workflow Runtime Services
components.description: Infrastructure implementations for starting workflows, executing metadata-driven transitions, reading context, and inspecting runtime state.

components.name: SLA Monitor Service
components.description: Operational service behind the run-sla command. Finds overdue pending tasks and queues SlaTaskOverdue notifications once per task.

components.name: Notification Outbox Processor
components.description: Processes pending NotificationOutbox rows, leases each row, calls the configured INotificationSender, and marks successful deliveries Sent.

components.name: EF Core Persistence
components.description: WorkflowDbContext, entities, migrations, seed data, and seed verification for workflow metadata and runtime records.

components.name: SQL Server Database
components.description: SQL-backed source of truth for workflow definitions, transitions, instances, tasks, SLA policies, notifications, idempotency records, mock section data, and audit history.

components.name: Notification Senders
components.description: Configured notification delivery abstraction. Console and NoOp are local implementations; SMTP uses MailKit and Smtp:RoleEmailMap configuration.

components.name: External SMTP Relay
components.description: Optional on-prem SMTP relay target used only when Notifications:Sender is Smtp and Smtp:Host/Smtp:From are configured.

components.name: Desktop Packager
components.description: Placeholder for a ToDesktop or desktop packaging system. No implementation or config was found in this repository.
sourceHints: No ToDesktop/app.todesktop/Electron/Tauri files found by repository search

workflows.name: Invite new user
workflows.description: Documents the likely integration path for a user invitation workflow. Repository inspection did not find invitation controllers, DTOs, entities, or identity-provider calls.
notes: No InviteUser, Invitation, UserInvite, or invite endpoint was found.
PROJECT.md explicitly forbids adding DemoUser tables and SQL user-to-role mapping in v1.
If this workflow is added later, it should stay outside the reusable workflow engine unless it is modeled as metadata-driven workflow action data.

steps.label: Invite request DTO
steps.details: A future form or admin UI would send an invitation request to a new API endpoint. This endpoint does not exist today.

steps.label: Caller identity and workflow roles
steps.details: Existing API requests resolve the caller through ClaimsWorkflowActorResolver. This verifies who is calling; it does not create or invite users.

steps.label: Invitation contract missing
steps.details: The current contracts cover workflow action envelopes, context, available actions, and action results. No invitation contract was found.

steps.label: No user persistence path
steps.details: The EF model persists workflow metadata/runtime data only. It intentionally does not include a DemoUser table or SQL role mapping.

steps.label: Invite email would use sender abstraction
steps.details: If invitation email is added, the closest existing delivery mechanism is INotificationSender via the outbox processor. That is an inferred extension, not current behavior.

workflows.name: ToDesktop build
workflows.description: Shows the likely build/package path using the repository's actual .NET solution, CI, and source bundle scripts. No ToDesktop-specific configuration was found.
notes: Repository search found no ToDesktop/app.todesktop/Electron/Tauri assets.
The concrete build assets are dotnet restore/build/test, GitHub Actions, and cdt-src-bundle scripts.

steps.label: Build trigger
steps.details: A developer or CI job starts the build. The repo's actual automation is GitHub Actions plus source bundle scripts.

steps.label: Build console project
steps.details: The source solution includes the console proof of concept and builds it under .NET 10 with warnings treated as errors.

steps.label: Build API project
steps.details: The separate API solution builds the ASP.NET Core controller host that references the shared workflow projects.

steps.label: Compile shared application layer
steps.details: The console and API compile against the same contracts, validators, normalizers, command handlers, and result builders.

steps.label: Compile infrastructure and migrations
steps.details: The infrastructure project brings EF Core SQL Server, migrations, seed data, workflow services, SLA, and notification sender implementations into the build.

steps.label: Desktop packaging handoff
steps.details: If a ToDesktop package is introduced, this is where build/publish artifacts would be handed to it. This handoff is not implemented in the current repo.

workflows.name: Portfolio Trade: Submit for Checker
workflows.description: Maker submits a Portfolio Trade from Draft to CheckerReview. The engine saves section data, changes state from SQL metadata, creates a Checker task with SLA, queues a notification, writes audit, and stores idempotency replay data.

steps.label: execute-json sample envelope
steps.details: The console command reads 02-submit-for-checker.json and dispatches ExecuteJsonCommandHandler.

steps.label: Validate, normalize, and hash request
steps.details: The application layer validates required envelope shape, normalizes overrides/idempotency values, and computes a canonical request hash.

steps.label: WorkflowExecutionRequest
steps.details: Application calls IWorkflowExecutionService.Execute with the normalized envelope, request hash, and admin override flag.

steps.label: Load metadata and current runtime state
steps.details: The runtime checks idempotency, loads WorkflowInstance, verifies expected state/version/task, resolves active action metadata, and selects a transition by fromState/actionKey/allowedRole.

steps.label: Atomic EF transaction
steps.details: EF saves mock section data, updates instance state/version, creates CheckerReviewTask, queues WorkflowTaskAssigned, writes audit, and adds idempotency replay data.

steps.label: Persist runtime rows
steps.details: SQL Server stores the updated workflow state, task, outbox notification, audit row, mock section data, and idempotency record.

steps.label: WorkflowActionResultEnvelope
steps.details: The result summarizes the old/new state, created task, queued notification, audit write, request hash, diagnostics, and refreshed workflow context.

workflows.name: API: Execute workflow action
workflows.description: HTTP version of a button-click workflow action. The API stamps actor information from claims, enforces route/body identity, validates the envelope, executes the same reusable workflow service, and maps result codes to HTTP responses.

steps.label: POST WorkflowActionEnvelope
steps.details: A client posts the action envelope to WorkflowActionsController. The route workflowInstanceId must match the body when the body supplies one.

steps.label: Resolve actor
steps.details: The controller resolves the caller from authenticated claims or development headers, then overwrites envelope.actor with the trusted server-side actor.

steps.label: Normalize, validate, hash
steps.details: The controller uses the same application helpers as the console path before calling the execution service.

steps.label: Execute transition
steps.details: The reusable workflow runtime performs the same metadata-driven transition path used by execute-json.

steps.label: SQL writes and metadata reads
steps.details: The runtime reads transition metadata and writes section data, state/task changes, outbox rows, audit, and idempotency records as needed.

steps.label: Map result to HTTP
steps.details: WorkflowHttpResultMapper turns result codes into API responses while preserving the standard WorkflowActionResultEnvelope body.

workflows.name: Open form: workflow context
workflows.description: When a user opens a form, the API or console reads persisted workflow state, pending task, SLA status, and metadata-derived available actions for that actor.

steps.label: GET workflow context
steps.details: A future form UI can request workflow context from WorkflowContextController.

steps.label: Resolve user and roles
steps.details: The API resolves the current actor and passes user id plus roles to WorkflowContextReader.

steps.label: WorkflowContextReadRequest
steps.details: The controller calls IWorkflowContextReader.Read. The console show-context command reaches the same reader through application command handlers.

steps.label: Read state, task, SLA, actions
steps.details: The reader loads WorkflowInstance, definition version, current state definition, pending task, task definition, and role-matching transition/action metadata.

steps.label: WorkflowContextResponse
steps.details: The response tells the UI current state, task, SLA, actor access, and available actions with requestDefaults for the next button click.

workflows.name: SLA overdue notification
workflows.description: run-sla scans active pending tasks with due dates and queues one SlaTaskOverdue notification per overdue task. process-notification-outbox later sends pending rows through the configured sender.

steps.label: run-sla command
steps.details: An operator runs the console command, optionally passing --now for deterministic tests and demos.

steps.label: IRunSlaService.RunAsync
steps.details: The command handler calls RunSlaService with the effective time.

steps.label: Find overdue active tasks
steps.details: The service queries pending WorkflowTask rows with DueAtUtc before the scan time, joined to active WorkflowInstance rows, and skips tasks that already have SlaTaskOverdue outbox rows.

steps.label: Queue SlaTaskOverdue
steps.details: For each overdue task, EF inserts a Pending NotificationOutbox row with notification type SlaTaskOverdue and recipient role from route or task assignment.

steps.label: process-notification-outbox command
steps.details: A separate operational command processes pending notifications. In the current repo this is command-driven, not a hosted background loop.

steps.label: Process pending rows
steps.details: The processor claims each row with a lease token, calls the configured sender, and marks success as Sent. On send failure it releases the row back to Pending and records LastError.

steps.label: NotificationDelivery
steps.details: The processor sends a NotificationDelivery through Console, NoOp, or SMTP based on Notifications:Sender configuration.

steps.label: SMTP email (optional)
steps.details: When Smtp is configured, SmtpNotificationSender builds a MailKit message, resolves role recipients from Smtp:RoleEmailMap or RecipientOverride, sends, and disconnects.

workflows.name: Initialize and verify seed data
workflows.description: init-db applies EF Core migrations and Portfolio Trade seed metadata. verify-seed validates that required states, roles, actions, transitions, task definitions, SLA policies, and routes exist.

steps.label: init-db command
steps.details: The console dispatches init-db through CommandRegistry to the registered database initializer.

steps.label: Apply migrations and seed
steps.details: WorkflowDatabaseInitializer applies migrations and invokes WorkflowSeedService/PortfolioTradeSeedData.

steps.label: Persist metadata rows
steps.details: SQL Server stores the Portfolio Trade workflow definition, version, states, roles, actions, transitions, task definitions, SLA policies, and notification routes.

steps.label: verify-seed command
steps.details: The console dispatches verify-seed to SeedVerificationService.

steps.label: Validate required metadata
steps.details: Seed verification reads SQL metadata and fails if required Portfolio Trade seed rows are missing.
